narrative_commentary: Year-on-year change in retail prices across a national basket of goods and services, the RBI's primary policy anchor. Base year 2024=100.
research_notes: Aug 2026 provisional; July 2026 now final at 4.45%. Food inflation (CFPI) 5.95%. Next release date stated in the press note itself.

narrative_commentary: Year-on-year change in wholesale prices of goods, an early signal of input-cost pressure feeding into retail inflation. Base year 2022-23.
source_label: Office of the Economic Adviser — WPI Press Release
research_notes: Fuel and Power inflation 22.93% (from 20.05%) is the main driver. All-commodities index 110.8 vs 110.0.

narrative_commentary: Gross Goods and Services Tax collected in the month, reflecting the previous month's business activity. A high-frequency proxy for domestic demand and formal-sector activity.
research_notes: previous_value is the year-ago comparable (Aug 2025), not July 2026, because GST is reported on a YoY basis. Aug 2025 was REVISED DOWN from Rs 1.86 lakh crore to Rs 1.74 lakh crore. Net GST Aug 2026 = Rs 1,68,057 crore (+8.3% YoY).

narrative_commentary: Survey-based index of factory activity. Readings above 50 signal expansion versus the previous month; the level indicates the pace of change, not output volume.
source_label: S&P Global — HSBC India Manufacturing PMI
research_notes: Privately compiled (S&P Global/HSBC), not government data. Final 52.8, weakest since Aug 2021; some aggregators still show the 52.9 flash estimate. Official release page is paywalled/indexed only at spglobal PMI hub. HSBC flash PMI for September scheduled for release on 23 Sep 2026 (not yet out at run time); final due 1 Oct / 5 Oct.

narrative_commentary: Survey-based index of services-sector activity, India's largest output segment. Above 50 signals month-on-month expansion.
source_label: S&P Global — HSBC India Services PMI
research_notes: Privately compiled. Final 54.1, revised down from 54.5 flash. Could not open the S&P Global press release directly; value cross-checked across multiple reports. HSBC flash PMI for September scheduled for release on 23 Sep 2026 (not yet out at run time); final due 1 Oct / 5 Oct.

narrative_commentary: Gap between goods exports and goods imports in the month. A narrowing deficit eases pressure on the external account and the rupee.
source_label: Ministry of Commerce & Industry — Monthly Trade Data
research_notes: Exports $43.18 bn (+26.12% YoY), imports $72.67 bn (+14.1% YoY). Commerce Ministry press release PDF not retrievable; figures cross-checked against Reuters and Commerce Secretary briefing. Note tradestat portal landing page still shows FY2025-26 as latest dataset.

narrative_commentary: Year-on-year growth in industrial output across mining, manufacturing, electricity and water supply. Index level was 124.8 in the reference month.
research_notes: Quick Estimate. June 2026 was REVISED UP from 7.3% (quick estimate) to 8.8%; delta uses the revised June figure. Mining contracted 0.9%. Next release date from MoSPI Advance Release Calendar 2026-27 (IIP for Aug 2026 on 28 Sep).

indicator_title: Core Sector Output (Index of Core Industries)
narrative_commentary: Combined output growth of nine core infrastructure industries (coal, crude oil, natural gas, refinery products, fertilizers, steel, cement, electricity and iron ore), which carry a large share of the IIP weight. Base year 2022-23.
source_label: Office of the Economic Adviser — Index of Core Industries Press Release
research_notes: Aug 2026 provisional; index 119.2. July 2026 final revised DOWN to 5.0% (index 120.8) from 5.4% provisional; delta uses revised July. Growth in cement 12.5%, electricity 11.6%, iron ore 5.5%, steel 3.4%, refinery products 2.6%; contraction in coal -3.8%, natural gas -4.9%, crude oil -3.6%, fertilizers -12.4%. Apr-Aug cumulative 4.3%. Title updated to reflect the nine-industry series. Next release date stated in the press note.

narrative_commentary: Total RBI-held foreign currency assets, gold, SDRs and IMF reserve position. The buffer available to absorb external shocks and smooth rupee volatility.
research_notes: Small decline from the all-time high of $785.706 bn (week ended 4 Sep), which itself was a record $44.9 bn weekly jump. FCA fell $2.372 bn to $645.796 bn. RBI WSS viewer is JS-gated and could not be read directly; figures cross-checked against CNBC-TV18, ET BFSI and Trading Economics reporting of the same RBI release.

narrative_commentary: Broad money: currency with the public plus bank deposits and other deposits with the RBI. Rapid growth can signal liquidity build-up ahead of price pressure.
research_notes: Jump from 14.2% to 16.7% in one fortnight is unusually large — verify against the RBI WSS Table 4 before publishing. M3 outstanding around Rs 3.32 crore crore (Rs 332 lakh crore). RBI WSS could not be opened directly.

target_anchor: MacroNest anchor: credit growth aligned with deposit growth
narrative_commentary: Year-on-year growth in outstanding credit of scheduled commercial banks, a direct read on transmission of monetary policy into the real economy.
research_notes: Conflict resolved: 19.1% refers to the fortnight ended 31 Aug (not 4 Sep). Outstanding ~₹223.9 lakh crore; credit rose ~₹3.8 trillion in the fortnight. Previous 18.3% at 15 Aug (Mint rounds it to 18%). Cross-checked across Business Standard, Mint and Deccan Chronicle. Data for 15 Sep fortnight due this week. RBI WSS not read directly.

target_anchor: MacroNest anchor: deposit growth keeping pace with credit
narrative_commentary: Year-on-year growth in aggregate deposits of scheduled commercial banks, the funding base for bank lending.
research_notes: Conflict resolved: 17.8% refers to the fortnight ended 31 Aug. Outstanding ~₹278.7 lakh crore; deposits rose ~₹9.4-9.5 trillion in the fortnight, driven by FCNR(B) inflows before RBI's concessional swap window closed on 31 Aug. Previous 14.7% at 15 Aug. Cross-checked across Business Standard, Rediff and Mint. RBI WSS not read directly.

narrative_commentary: The rate at which the RBI lends overnight to banks against government securities. The benchmark policy rate that anchors all other lending rates in the system.
research_notes: Unanimous 6-0 hold; fourth consecutive pause. SDF 5.00%, MSF and Bank Rate 5.50%, stance neutral. Next MPC scheduled 5-7 Oct 2026 with the resolution on 7 Oct. RBI press release listing page returns stale cached content; verify the resolution URL before publishing.

typical_release_window: Last working day of the second month after quarter end
narrative_commentary: Year-on-year growth in real gross domestic product at constant 2022-23 prices. The headline measure of aggregate economic output.
research_notes: previous_value is the year-ago quarter growth rate (Q1 FY2025-26 = 6.9%), the economically appropriate comparison for a YoY growth series, not the sequential quarter. Real GVA +8.2%, nominal GDP +10.3%, real GDP Rs 81.36 lakh crore. Beat RBI's 7.0% projection.

target_anchor: MacroNest anchor: CAD below 2% of GDP
narrative_commentary: Net balance on trade in goods and services plus income and transfers, expressed as a share of GDP. A contained deficit signals a sustainable external position.
source_label: RBI — Developments in India's Balance of Payments
research_notes: CAD $4.2 bn (0.5% of GDP) vs $3.4 bn (0.4%, revised) a year earlier; merchandise trade deficit widened to $86.1 bn from $68.9 bn. One secondary outlet reported $3.1 bn for the same quarter — treated as erroneous since Reuters, PTI and ANI all quote the RBI release at $4.2 bn. RBI press release listing page returned stale cache; link the specific BoP release when available.

narrative_commentary: RBI's official daily reference rate for the rupee against the US dollar, used as the benchmark for settlement and valuation.
source_label: FBIL reference rate (via NSE RBI Reference Rate Statistics)
research_notes: 22 Sep 2026 reference rate 95.8179 (GBP 128.1223, EUR 109.8252, JPY100 60.79); 21 Sep 95.7991; 18 Sep 95.7910. Delta now available. Interbank spot closed stronger at ~95.58 provisional on 22 Sep, so the reference rate (fixed ~1:30 PM) and close diverge. Row was previously held back only for the missing delta — ready to review for publish.

typical_release_window: Business days (FBIL par yield curve, ~6:00 PM)
narrative_commentary: Benchmark yield on ten-year Government of India securities, the reference rate for long-term borrowing costs across the economy.
research_notes: Market close 22 Sep 7.016% vs 7.054% on 21 Sep (Investing.com); Trading Economics shows 7.04% (-0.03) for the same day, so size of the fall differs slightly between sources. Up ~56 bps YoY. Official FBIL par yield file not read directly — confirm before publishing.

narrative_commentary: Closing level of the NSE's 50-stock benchmark index, the standard gauge of large-cap Indian equity performance.
research_notes: Weekly F&O expiry day; indicative price dipped ~1% intraday before recovering. 21 Sep close 23414.30 (+67.90). NSE site bot-gated; cross-checked against Moneycontrol, Economic Times and Business Standard.

narrative_commentary: Closing level of the BSE's 30-stock benchmark index, the longest-running headline gauge of Indian equity market sentiment.
research_notes: 21 Sep close 74858.99 (+564.03) after six weekly declines; gave back 330 pts on 22 Sep. Cross-checked across Business Standard and Economic Times.

target_anchor: MacroNest anchor: below 15 indicates calm markets
narrative_commentary: Expected 30-day volatility of the Nifty 50 implied by index option prices. Lower readings indicate calmer expectations, higher readings signal stress.
research_notes: Falling volatility is read as economically positive, hence badge 'positive' despite trend_direction 'down'. Day range 10.62-11.41; 52-week range 8.72-28.91. NSE page bot-gated; cross-checked against Upstox and Anand Rathi.

narrative_commentary: Net purchases minus sales of Indian equities and debt by foreign portfolio investors, a high-frequency read on external risk appetite towards India.
research_notes: Now populated from NSDL-based PTI weekly summary (The Hindu, Times of India, NDTV Profit): equity MTD -₹20,974 crore to 18 Sep vs -₹13,138 crore a week earlier. Debt also negative (FAR -₹10,296 cr, VRR -₹1,817 cr). CY2026 equity outflow ~₹2.45 lakh crore. Exchange provisional FII cash data since then: -₹576 cr (21 Sep), -₹3,810 cr (22 Sep). Still one syndicated source and NSDL page not read directly — verify before publishing.

narrative_commentary: Share of the labour force aged 15 and above that is unemployed, measured on the Current Weekly Status basis in the monthly PLFS bulletin.
research_notes: Rural UR 4.1% (lowest since Jan 2026), urban UR 6.8% (up from 6.7%). LFPR rose to 55.6% from 55.4%, WPR to 52.8% from 52.5%. Next release date from MoSPI Advance Release Calendar 2026-27.

typical_release_window: Daily (Department of Consumer Affairs price monitoring)
target_anchor: MacroNest anchor: early warning for food inflation
narrative_commentary: Daily retail prices of key food items collected across reporting centres, used as an early signal of food-price pressure ahead of the monthly CPI.
source_label: Dept. of Consumer Affairs — Price Monitoring Division
research_notes: LEFT BLANK DELIBERATELY. This is a multi-commodity dashboard with no single headline number; MacroNest needs to decide which item or composite to track (e.g. all-India modal price of tomato/onion/pulses) before it can be populated. DCA portal is dynamic and was not machine-readable in this run.

stance_state: Tightening resumed, one more hike signalled
typical_release_window: After each FOMC meeting (8 per year, ~11:30 PM IST)
narrative_commentary: The US Federal Reserve's policy rate range. It drives global dollar liquidity, US bond yields and foreign portfolio flows into emerging markets like India.
research_notes: Unanimous 12-0 vote to raise by 25 bps to 3.75-4.00%, first hike since 2023; projections point to possibly one more hike this year (CNBC). Next FOMC 27-28 Oct, decision 28 Oct (Fed calendar). Hike cited as a driver of September FPI selling from India.

narrative_commentary: Year-on-year change in US consumer prices (CPI-U). The key input into Federal Reserve rate decisions and global rate expectations.
source_label: US Bureau of Labor Statistics — CPI News Release
research_notes: Headline +0.4% MoM SA (July +0.1%). Core CPI 2.4% YoY (from 2.5%), +0.3% MoM. September CPI scheduled 14 Oct 2026, 8:30 AM ET.

typical_release_window: First Friday of month (~6:00 PM IST)
narrative_commentary: Monthly change in US non-farm employment, the headline read on the strength of the world's largest economy.
source_label: US Bureau of Labor Statistics — Employment Situation
research_notes: Consensus was ~53-56k. July revised up from -23k to +21k; previous_value uses revised July. Subject to revision in the next two reports.

typical_release_window: First Friday of month (~6:00 PM IST)
narrative_commentary: Share of the US labour force that is unemployed (U-3). Together with inflation, it frames the Federal Reserve's dual mandate.
source_label: US Bureau of Labor Statistics — Employment Situation
research_notes: Unemployed persons ~7.0 million, little changed over the year.

narrative_commentary: Yield on the benchmark 10-year US government bond, the global reference for long-term borrowing costs. Higher US yields tend to pull money out of emerging markets.
source_label: Federal Reserve — H.15 Selected Interest Rates
research_notes: Constant-maturity series; 18 Sep 5.01%, 21 Sep 4.96%. Intraday 22 Sep market quotes ~4.93% (WSJ/Trading Economics) — official 22 Sep print due 23 Sep. ~0.8 pp higher than a year ago.

narrative_commentary: Value of the US dollar against a basket of six major currencies. A stronger dollar typically weighs on the rupee and emerging-market assets.
research_notes: Cross-checked against Investing.com (22 Sep close 100.54, +0.11%). Up ~1.4% over the past month. Badge 'warning' reflects pressure on the rupee.

target_anchor: MacroNest anchor: below $90/bbl eases India's import bill
narrative_commentary: Price of the global benchmark crude oil. India imports most of its oil, so Brent directly affects inflation, the trade deficit and the rupee.
source_label: ICE Brent futures (via FT Markets Data)
research_notes: Falling from 108.75 on 15 Sep on hopes of US-Iran talks. Intraday range 97.43-102.30 on 22 Sep; late-session quotes differ by source (Trading Economics ~98.6-101.8), so settlement vs close timing matters. Badge 'positive' because lower oil helps India.

typical_release_window: Trading days (LBMA PM fix ~8:30 PM IST)
narrative_commentary: International spot gold price. A safe-haven asset and a large item in India's import bill and household savings.
research_notes: Spot quotes for 22 Sep differ across sources ($4,317-$4,362); LBMA PM fix (the official benchmark) is licensed and not readable. Last week LBMA PM ended at ~$4,348 (Scrapmonster). Take the LBMA PM fix before publishing.

typical_release_window: After each ECB Governing Council meeting (~5:45 PM IST)
narrative_commentary: The European Central Bank's main policy rate for the euro area, the second-largest bloc of global monetary policy after the Fed.
source_label: European Central Bank — Monetary Policy Decisions
research_notes: All three key rates raised 25 bps: deposit 2.50%, MRO 2.65%, MLF 2.90%, effective 16 Sep 2026. Next monetary policy meeting 28-29 Oct (ECB calendar).

typical_release_window: Last day of month (~7:00 AM IST)
narrative_commentary: National Bureau of Statistics survey of Chinese factory activity. A read on demand in the world's second-largest economy and on global commodity prices.
source_label: National Bureau of Statistics of China — PMI Release
research_notes: Still below 50 but improving; output (50.4) and new orders (50.6) returned to expansion. Large enterprises 50.6. Next release 30 Sep 2026.
